tellings.difference: Puts it in the 1950s rather than the 1960s, names Guidance Technologies, and casts Lear as a witness of Brown's experiments rather than recalling lunches at a diner.
tellings.link_reason: Both are about Bill Lear's office sitting right across the street from Brown's Santa Monica operation, so the two men were neighbours.

as_told.title: Bill Lear as neighbor and witness of Brown's experiments

plain: A scientist named Townsend Brown, the subject of a documentary that calls him a CIA scientist who built UFOs, is said to have worked right across the street from the inventor Bill Lear in Santa Monica, California. Linda Brown, who speaks from her own memory, recalls that they "used to walk across" to a little diner right across the street, placing this in the 1960s. Michels tells it differently in another episode: he says Lear's office stood across from Brown's company, Guidance Technologies, in the 1950s, and he casts Lear as someone who witnessed Brown's experiments rather than a lunch companion. The two tellings agree on the closeness but not on the decade. The point, for the tellers, is that a well-known inventor may have seen Brown's work up close.
